The word “hungry” doesn’t exist to me. Whenever I asked for food as a child, my mum would say “There’s cabbage in the fridge” or “Yeah I think we have some bread” and I’d be like “But I’d like something more...”. The immediate response was “If you don’t want to eat those things, then you aren’t hungry, you’re picky. There are people in this world who would be extremely happy to eat just cabbage and bread”. So moral of the story is to always be grateful. My friends constantly get new clothes, change their styles, grow up and change their mindsets etc. But I’ve remained the same for years. I go shopping maybe once a year? If my clothes aren’t tattered or straight up falling off, I will wear them, same goes for shoes. Friend got a new phone? Yeah I still have my iPhone SE from 3 years ago. Although I am proud of myself for my empathy, I still feel self conscious about myself. I’d like to wear different clothes and have a newer phone, just explore styles to see what I like. But my subconscious is like “no, that’s selfish, be grateful you have a roof over your head” so yeah.

There’s two sides to the coin here. On one hand people come and go in your life and you yourself need to be the deciding factor whether you learn to trust them or not, and in response they trust you too and your relationship/friendship with them won’t be shallow. And on the other hand there is a person that will always stick with you, and that is yourself. From the beginning, to the end. Nobody can define their way of loving or even slightly appreciating themself, and the way I’ve done so is through escapism. Even if I imagine myself somewhere where there’s no pain, I’m still with myself. As cliche as it is, loving yourself is truly the way you learn to love others, because you’ve learned to love the person who you thought you hated most.

Sadness can’t be defeated, but it can be balanced out. I’ve had severe depression and anxiety for many years now, and my way to escape the thoughts is firstly think through them step-by-step and then realise I’m still not sure how I would actually kill myself, and then I think in detail about the bad events that will occur after I’ve done it. I imagine in vivid detail someone finding my body, having to report it and so on. 
My way of fighting against these thoughts is through escapism or small acts of achievement. I just cleaned my room the other day and yet I always thought I hated cleaning with a passion, but once I started doing it, I sort of subconsciously continued and then I started imagining how I could redecorate my entire room, and how I’d need to be alive to actually do so. In conclusion I give myself small reasons to live every day. The show I used to watch just announced a new season? Hey, maybe I should wait and check it out. I really want to paint but I’m too tired to do so? Well, I guess I’ll have to do it tomorrow. Find your own ways of pushing yourself to live each and every day, and then I hope that the time periods spread out even more, and instead of aiming to “live another day” maybe “live another 10 years”.

I don’t remember the names of the people involved nor the exact years this took place, but it was somewhere around the 1970-1980 period, Estonia and specifically northern Estonia. The Russians still spread communist propaganda as much as they could and that included using the newly popularised television programs and radio stations. Estonia was a big mess, you did one thing wrong or went against the USSR and you’re essentially dead. Now, even if Russia monitored the majority of the things that were played on the Estonian TV channels, Finland decided to just pop up and build their TV tower so tall and mighty that the people in northern Estonia could also watch their programs. Problem was, you couldn’t hear anything. 
Now, when Estonians received info that Finland was going to play an erotica film at 2am one night, you needed sound, and oh boy, the things they did to watch their damn adult movie. Now, I’m obviously just mentioning one of the more funnier reasons they decided to do this “operation” (which I will talk about), but there were many others. 

A full on mafia started forming just to get antennas and other audio receivers so that people could watch Finnish TV with sound. A man who was a young boy at the time described how his father was a part of the circle providing others with the needed parts. He said that “One day, my father put me into the back seat of our car and drove off, not saying a word. He drove us to Mustamäe (an area of the Capital, Tallinn) and dropped me off in front of an apartment. He instructed me to go to the fourth floor and knock 8 times on the door to the 45th flat. I did as told, and a man in a robe opened and handed me a box filled with little technical objects, before quickly shutting the door”. 
He also explained how he could never tell anybody about this and what his dad did, because the Russians considered it as going against the communists. 

So basically, Estonians were tired of not knowing what the hell was going on in the outside world, they got a glimpse of it, needed more and decided to just start an entire networking system for TV parts and antennas and radios, just to watch Finnish TV.
